name: Lauderdale Lakes
intro: Lauderdale Lakes shares the 441 corridor's deep Caribbean food culture — Jamaican restaurants, island bakeries, and takeout kitchens serving one of the most concentrated West Indian communities in Florida — and adds a cluster of healthcare and senior-living facilities whose dining services need institutional consistency day after day.

Both halves get a purpose-built account. Restaurant kitchens order island staples — plantains, yams, callaloo when in, scotch bonnets, fresh thyme — in split cases that fit tight storage. Facility kitchens run scheduled case programs with reliable windows and the documentation their food-service contracts require. Everything rides the same refrigerated route, fifteen minutes out of Pompano Beach.
route_note: About 15 minutes from our Pompano Beach warehouse — an early stop on the central Broward morning run.

faqs_unique.q: Can you supply healthcare and senior facility kitchens in Lauderdale Lakes?
faqs_unique.a: Yes. Facility dining services run consistent case programs with scheduled delivery windows, steady specs, and menu-cycle planning.

faqs_unique.q: Do you stock West Indian produce for Lauderdale Lakes restaurants?
faqs_unique.a: Yes. Island staples — plantains, yams, scotch bonnets, thyme, and seasonal Caribbean produce — are available by the case or split case on daily routes.
